title: Find the Minimum Cost Array Permutation
summary: Given an array nums as a permutation of [0, 1, 2, ..., n-1], find the permutation perm that minimizes the score defined as the sum of absolute differences between consecutive elements and the corresponding elements in nums.
statement: Given an array nums as a permutation of [0, 1, 2, ..., n-1], find the permutation perm that minimizes the score defined as the sum of absolute differences between consecutive elements and the corresponding elements in nums. If there are multiple such permutations, return the lexicographically smallest one.
constraints: nums is a permutation of 0 through n-1 and n is at least two.
For permutation perm, score is sum of abs(perm[i]-nums[perm[(i+1) mod n]]) over all cyclic adjacent positions.
Return the lexicographically smallest permutation attaining the minimum score.
hints: Rotating a cyclic permutation does not change its score, so every optimum has a unique rotation beginning with zero.
Use subset DP keyed by visited mask and last value, then greedily choose the smallest next value that preserves optimal cost.
cost(mask,last)=min edge(last,next)+cost(mask+next,next); base adds closing edge to zero; reconstruct ascending.
The recurrence enumerates every normalized cyclic order, and ascending optimal reconstruction supplies the lexicographically smallest minimizer.
editorial: The recurrence enumerates every normalized cyclic order, and ascending optimal reconstruction supplies the lexicographically smallest minimizer.

tests.explanation: The normalized order [0,1,2] has score two and is the lexicographically smallest minimum-cost permutation.
Among cyclic orders beginning with zero, [0,2,1] has the minimum score and is lexicographically first.
